children: named Klaus Zellmer as its next president and chief executive, setting up another leadership change as the Swedish automaker tries to improve sales and profitability.

Zellmer will assume the role no later than Oct. 1, 2027. He will succeed Hakan Samuelsson, who returned for a second stint as CEO in 2025. Samuelsson recently said he doesn’t intend to continue working full time after his contract expires in April.

For investors, the appointment adds clarity to Volvo’s succession plans but doesn’t resolve its immediate challenges. The Geely-controlled automaker is contending with U.S. tariffs, softer demand for electric vehicles, declining sales in China and elevated development costs. Its shares have fallen more than 45% this year and remain near record lows.

recently announced plans to introduce 13 models by 2030 as it seeks to double its market share. The company also must separate aspects of its Western and Chinese technology operations to preserve access to the U.S. market, where sister brand Polestar faces sales restrictions.
Zellmer will inherit responsibility for turning that ambitious product strategy into stronger sales, improved margins and a recovery in Volvo’s battered stock.

title: Volvo names Klaus Zellmer as next CEO amid turnaround push
